Squash(squash::SquashArgs),

    /// Merge sources into a target commit, keeping its change, with -s
    #[command(long_about = "\
        Give one target commit the sources named as its parents, in order,\n\
        keeping the target's own change, description, and change id, so its\n\
        trailer stays right. The target's tree becomes the merge of the\n\
        sources with its own change applied, `jj rebase -r <target> -o\n\
        <s1> -o <s2> ...`.\n\n\
        One target, typically @, and N sources, anything: a bookmark, main,\n\
        a change id, an earlier merge, a root. A cycle's closing is\n\
        --target @ --from main --from @-, which `commit --closing` runs, and\n\
        one --from makes the target linear again, the undo.\n\n\
        -s is required: `w` the work repo or `p` a plain repo, the agent\n\
        repo never holding a merge. Refused: a source at or below the target\n\
        and a published target. Reported: a conflicted result.")]
    Merge(merge::MergeArgs),
//!   the work repo. The agent side's `@` is the session's journal
//!   and is committed as it stands.
//! - `--closing` makes the work commit the cycle's merge close-out:
//!   `@`, the closing's edits, is first given `main` and the last
//!   rung as its parents, as `vc-x1 merge --target @ --from main
//!   --from @-` does, then committed, which keeps them. `main` is
//!   wherever it is now, so one that moved during the cycle is
//!   joined by the merge rather than needing a rebase.
//!   The title's " closing" or " dead-end closing" suffix is checked
}

/// Merge `main` and the last rung into `@`, the closing's edits, as
/// `vc-x1 merge --target @ --from main --from @-` does, before the
/// commit, which keeps `@`'s parents.
125:vc-x1 merge -s w --target T --from S...    # Merge sources into a target, keeping its change
1593:### merge
1603:vc-x1 merge -s w --target @ --from A --from B          # two lines of work into @
1604:vc-x1 merge -s w --target @ --from main --from @-      # a cycle's closing, as commit --closing does
1605:vc-x1 merge -s w --target @- --from @--                # the target linear again, the undo
1606:vc-x1 merge -s w --target @ --from main --dry-run      # say what it would do
  trailers, the one sanctioned re-describe of a trailer-carrying commit.
- `vc-x1 push` only publishes: the work bookmark `@-` sits on, and the agent-repo's `main`. Its
  agent half folds the agent `@` first, the journal's last lines, and its work half refuses a
  non-empty `@`, which is a `squash` or the next rung, the user's call. `--title`, `--body`, and the
  bookmark argument go, the bookmark inferred from `@-` and named only as a check.
- `vc-x1 squash-push` stays, wink's most-used command, `squash-push -s a` the agent half of a push
  on its own, and `-s w|b` the fold-and-publish that asks nothing.
- `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <s1> --from <s2>...` gives one unpublished target the
  sources as its parents, with jj's rebase meaning, and one `--from` makes it linear again.
  `vc-x1 commit -s b --closing` is `merge --target @ --from main --from @-` and then the commit:
  the closing as the merge close-out, its first parent the current `main`, its second the last
  rung. The " closing" and " dead-end closing" title suffixes are checked against the flag, never
  its trigger.
- `vc-x1 install` runs `[install] release` after checking that `@-` is `main` at `main@origin`,
  `@` is empty, and the version is bare, and `vc-x1 install --dev` runs `[install] dev` with no
  check, the mid-cycle refresh of the dev binary.
  - It passes `dry_run: false`, since push's own dry run stops before it.

##### feat: vc-x1 merge, and commit --closing on it

The closing is made as the merge of the trunk and the ladder when it is committed, so no reshape
follows its review, by a primitive that merges any sources into any unpublished commit, and undoes
it.

* Making a commit and giving it several parents are separate operations, wink's point at this
  rung's review.
  - `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <s1> --from <s2>...` gives one target the sources as
    its parents, in order, keeping its change, description, and change id. One target and N
    sources, no assumption about where either lives, wink's model (2026-10-20): two lines of work
    merged into one commit, piecemeal merges onto other bookmarks, a root as a source. One
    `--from` makes the target linear again, the undo that lets a cycle be extended after its
    closing. All three flags are required, the target typically `@`.
* Keeping the target's tree and swapping its parents is right for one ladder only.
  - The first version did that, and with several sources the merge would have silently reverted
    all but one. The verb has jj's rebase meaning, the new tree the merge of the sources with the
    target's own change, which a test of two sources checks.
* Limits that are not artificial.
  - Refused: a source at or below the target, a cycle, and a published target, a remote rewrite.
    Reported and allowed: a conflicted result, left conflicted as jj leaves it, push refusing a
    conflicted repo anyway. A source that is an ancestor of another was going to be warned about
    as redundant, until the dogfood dry run of a closing warned: `main` below the last rung is
    the no-fast-forward shape a closing is, so it is unremarked.
    `-s a` and `-s b` are refused, the agent repo never holding a merge.
* The name, wink's: "reparent" read as an operation on one commit's parent, and "trapezoid" names
  only some results, a closing on one rung being a triangle. `merge` names the result.
* `commit --closing` is `merge --target @ --from main --from @-`, then the commit.
  - It merges before committing, so `@`'s parents are set and the commit keeps them, and `main`
    is the current one, not the fork point, so a `main` that moved during the cycle is joined by
    the merge rather than needing a rebase first, which a test checks. The title's " closing"
    suffix is checked against the flag both ways, and with no ladder, a single-step cycle, a
    " closing" title is just a title and `--closing` is refused.
  - A test makes the closing on a ladder of two rungs and folds a review fix into it with
    `squash`, which keeps both parents.
* Dry runs.
  - `commit --closing --dry-run` says which commits the closing would join, and `merge
    --dry-run` the parents it would give.

##### feat: vc-x1 install promotes main

The promotion is a subcommand that checks it is installing pushed `main` at a bare version, the
check the `build.rs` guard the opening removed could not make, and `--dev` is the dev install on
demand.

##### feat: vc-x1 run-dev runs the dev binary

The dev binary, off the PATH, is run through the config, with a warning when it is not the
manifest's version.

##### feat: vc-x1 merge, and commit --closing on it

The closing is made as the merge of the trunk and the ladder when it is committed, so no reshape
follows its review, by a primitive that merges any sources into any unpublished commit, and undoes
it.

* Making a commit and giving it several parents are separate operations, wink's point at this
  rung's review.
  - `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <s1> --from <s2>...` gives one target the sources as
    its parents, in order, keeping its change, description, and change id. One target and N
    sources, no assumption about where either lives, wink's model (2026-10-20): two lines of work
    merged into one commit, piecemeal merges onto other bookmarks, a root as a source. One
    `--from` makes the target linear again, the undo that lets a cycle be extended after its
    closing. All three flags are required, the target typically `@`.

  - The first version did that, and with several sources the merge would have silently reverted
    all but one. The verb has jj's rebase meaning, the new tree the merge of the sources with the
    target's own change, which a test of two sources checks.

  - Refused: a source at or below the target, a cycle, and a published target, a remote rewrite.
    Reported and allowed: a conflicted result, left conflicted as jj leaves it, push refusing a
    conflicted repo anyway. A source that is an ancestor of another was going to be warned about
    as redundant, until the dogfood dry run of a closing warned: `main` below the last rung is
    the no-fast-forward shape a closing is, so it is unremarked.
    `-s a` and `-s b` are refused, the agent repo never holding a merge.

### merge

Give one target commit the sources named as its parents, in order, keeping the target's own change,
description, and change id, so its trailer stays right. The target's tree becomes the merge of the
sources with its own change applied, `jj rebase -r <target> -o <s1> -o <s2> ...`. One target and N
sources, with no assumption about where either lives: the target is typically `@`, and a source
is anything, a bookmark, `main`, a change id, an earlier merge, a root, part of a set merged
piecemeal elsewhere.

```
vc-x1 merge -s w --target @ --from A --from B          # two lines of work into @
vc-x1 merge -s w --target @ --from main --from @-      # a cycle's closing, as commit --closing does
vc-x1 merge -s w --target @- --from @--                # the target linear again, the undo
vc-x1 merge -s w --target @ --from main --dry-run      # say what it would do
```

`-s`, `--target`, and `--from` are required, `-s` being `w` or `p`, since the agent repo never
holds a merge. Refused: a source that is the target or below it, a cycle, and a published target, a
remote rewrite. Reported and allowed: a conflicted result, left as jj leaves it with `jj resolve
--list` named. A source that is an ancestor of another, `main` below the last rung, is the
no-fast-forward shape a closing is, so it is neither refused nor reported.

### push

Publish a rung's pair. Push carries no description and writes none, so what was reviewed is what
goes out: `commit` makes the pair, the work commit and the agent commit each naming the other, or
the work half alone with its trailer naming the agent `@`, and push completes and publishes it.

```bash
vc-x1 push -s b                  # the pair, on the bookmark the work @- sits on
vc-x1 push -s b feature          # the same, the bookmark named as a check
vc-x1 push -s w                  # the work half only
vc-x1 push -s a                  # the agent half only, the remainder of a run that stopped

I made both of your review changes. `merge` now always adds, and it refuses only what jj itself treats as immutable. Full validation passed, and so did a fast run after the last edit (680 tests).

**What changed:**
- **Adding, not replacing:**
  - The sources go after the target's existing parents, and each `--from` is a revset that can name one or more commits.
  - Your ten-commit case now works one `merge` at a time, or as one `merge` with ten `--from`s, or with a single revset. All three give the same tree.
  - A source that is already a parent is skipped. A merge that adds nothing changes nothing and says so.
  - A revset's commits go in oldest first, and a revset that names no commit is refused.
- **On your loop point:** jj-lib's `rewrite::rebase_commit` takes the whole parent list, so vc-x1 adds all the sources in one call. That is one jj operation, and one `jj undo` takes it back. A loop of one-at-a-time merges ends with the same tree.
- **The undo changed:** with adding, one `--from` no longer makes a target linear again. `jj undo` or `jj rebase -r <target> -o ...` does that now, and the docs say so.
- **Immutability instead of "published":**
  - The target is refused only when it is in jj's `immutable()`, and `--ignore-immutable` overrides that.
  - vc-x1 runs revsets inside its own process with no jj aliases, so `immutable()` didn't exist there. The jj settings now include jj 0.46's built-in aliases, `trunk()` and `immutable()` among them, and your own `[revset-aliases]` override them as in `jj`.
  - A rung pushed to the cycle bookmark can now be merged into. The force-push after it still needs your approval.
- **`commit --closing`** still sets `@`'s parents to `[main, @-]`, trunk first. If it went through `merge` it would get `[@-, main]`, because `@-` is already a parent.
- **A git limit the tests hit:** git can't store a merge that has the root commit as a parent. Merging into a commit that sits directly on the root fails with jj's own error, and vc-x1 restores the repo.

**Tried with the dev binary on this repo:**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `--target @- --from main` | Accepted, though `@-` is pushed |
| `--target @ --from @-` | Nothing changes: already a parent |
| `--target main ...` | Refused as immutable, and names `--ignore-immutable` |
| `--target main ...` with `--ignore-immutable` | Passes that check, then refused as a cycle, since `@-` is above `main` |
| `--target main-` | Refused: the target must be one commit, and `main-` is two |

The rung record in `zDOING.md`, the README, and the long help describe the new form.

Today there's no way to name the target. It's fixed in each half:

- **Work half:** the target is always the work `@-`, the commit `commit` just made.
- **BOOKMARK** isn't a revset. It's one bookmark name, and the only thing it does is check. The name must be among the nearest bookmarks below `@-` (`heads(::@- & bookmarks())`), or push refuses. If you leave it out, push uses the bookmark of the line `@-` sits on, which is the usual case. So naming it never moves a bookmark anywhere `@-`'s line doesn't already lead.
- **Agent half:** the target is always the agent-repo's `main`, set to the partner commit, the agent commit the work commit's `ochid:` trailer names.

So push has no `--target` because it publishes "the pair just made", and that pins both ends.

**If we want a target**, here's the form I'd suggest, to match `merge`:
- **`--target REV`**, defaulting to `@-`: the work commit to publish. It must be exactly one commit and carry a trailer. With `-s w` it can be any such commit, and the bookmark is set to it.
- **WORK-BOOKMARK**, relabelled as you suggest, stays one name rather than a revset. A revset could name several bookmarks, and pointing several bookmarks at one target is hard to see as one push. The nearest-bookmark check would apply to the target instead of `@-`.
- **With `-s b`**, a target other than `@-` would be refused. The agent half folds the live journal into the partner, and that only makes sense for the rung just made. Publishing an older pair needs no agent half, since its partner is already in the journal's history.

This would be a change to push. Under the rules it's unplanned work, and you choose: a rung inserted after [9], or a `## Todo` entry for a later cycle. Nothing is changed yet, and rung [9] is still committed locally and waiting on the push.

The plain version: today push always publishes `@-`, and the bookmark name is only a safety check. We could add `--target`, defaulting to `@-`, and make the bookmark a plain name with a clearer label. I'd allow other targets only for the work half.

That splits it well. `push` stays "publish what's there", and moving a bookmark becomes its own verb, the way `merge` became its own verb apart from `commit`. Some thoughts:

- **jj already has the primitives.** `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` moves one named bookmark, and `jj bookmark move --from REVSET --to REV` moves whatever bookmarks sit at a revset. A vc-x1 wrapper earns its place by adding what jj doesn't check: the scope, a trailer on the target, the snapshot restore, and a dry run.
- **Naming:**
  - `--target <node>` matches `merge`, and `<node>` as "a bookmark or rev" comes for free, since a bookmark name is a revset that must name exactly one commit.
  - `--source <bookmark>` reads oddly next to `merge --from`, where the source is a commit. I'd suggest `--bookmark NAME`, required, or your WORK-BOOKMARK label. Your call.
- **Direction:** jj refuses to move a bookmark backward or sideways without `--allow-backwards`. I'd keep that refusal and the flag, as with `--ignore-immutable`. Moving forward along its line is the normal case.
- **Scope:** `-s w` and `-s p`, like `merge`. The agent-repo's `main` belongs to push's agent half, so `-s a` and `-s b` would be refused.
- **What it leaves push:** push would publish the work bookmark where it points, instead of setting it to `@-` itself. I'd keep push's default, setting it to `@-` and publishing, for the everyday rung, and use `move-bookmark` for the unusual case before a push.
- **Local only:** I'd have it never push, so every remote change still goes through `push` and your approval.

This is still unplanned work, so the same choice applies: a rung after [9], or a `## Todo` entry. Rung [9] is still committed locally, waiting on your go to push.

The plain version: a separate `move-bookmark --bookmark NAME --target REV` that moves a bookmark locally, checks what jj doesn't, and never pushes. Push keeps its everyday default and publishes wherever the bookmark points.

### feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev

(wink + agent, 2026-10-20, opened 2026-10-20) The code **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1** names: a
rung is committed locally before it is pushed, the closing is made as its trapezoid, the dev build
installs under its own root, and the promotion is a subcommand.

#### Problem

What the user reviews is not what is published. A rung's commit exists only once `vc-x1 push` has
made and published it, so a fix after the review of its description is a remote rewrite and a
squash-push in both repos. The closing is changed twice more after its review, at Land: the
package's plain name is squashed back into it, and the trapezoid recipe reshapes it into the merge.
The rename exists because a mid-cycle `cargo install` would otherwise replace the consumers'
binary, and Land's promotion itself names no command.

#### Solution

Provisional, the Todo's plan as filed:

- An `[install]` table in the config: `release`, the promotion,
  `["cargo install --path . --locked"]` here, `dev`, the dev install,
  `["cargo install --path . --locked --root tmp/dev"]` here, both lists like `[validate]`'s, and
  `dev-bin`, the dev install's binary, `"tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1"` here. `.vc-config.md`'s
  `[validate] full` ends with the dev install's line. The stale `vc-config.md` examples are fixed
  with the keys, fast's `["cargo test --bins"]`, full's `cargo test` without
  `-- --include-ignored`, and `test.fixtures`' `"../vc-x1-fixtures"` with its "skips with a notice"
  prose, and `vc-config-model.md` is regenerated.
- A scope resolver shared by `commit`, `squash`, `push`, `squash-push`, and `sync`: `-s`, required,
  one of `work|w`, `agent|a`, `both|b`, or `por|p`, a plain repo with no pair, and `-R` optional,
  the workspace by its root or either repo for `w|a|b`, the repo itself for `p`, the cwd without
  it. No `-s` is an error naming the four. `-s p` on a repo that is one side of a dual workspace is
  an error naming the side, and `-s w|a|b` on a directory with no workspace config is one.
- `vc-x1 commit -s b` makes the rung's commit pair from the two working copies, each stamped with
  the other's change id, with the given title and body. `-s w` and `-s a` are errors in a dual
  workspace, since a half is an unpaired commit, and `-s p` commits a plain repo with no trailer.
- `vc-x1 squash` folds each scoped working copy into its side of the pair, the review's fix into
  the work commit and the review's transcript into the agent commit, and refuses a side whose
  commit is published. With `--title` and `--body` it rewrites both descriptions and restamps the
  trailers, the one sanctioned re-describe of a trailer-carrying commit.
- `vc-x1 push` only publishes: the work bookmark `@-` sits on, and the agent-repo's `main`. Its
  agent half folds the agent `@` first, the journal's last lines, and its work half refuses a
  non-empty `@`, which is a `squash` or the next rung, the user's call. `--title`, `--body`, and the
  bookmark argument go, the bookmark inferred from `@-` and named only as a check.
- `vc-x1 squash-push` stays, wink's most-used command, `squash-push -s a` the agent half of a push
  on its own, and `-s w|b` the fold-and-publish that asks nothing.
- `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <revset>...` adds the sources to one target's parents,
  with jj's rebase meaning, refusing a target in jj's `immutable()` unless `--ignore-immutable`.
  `vc-x1 commit -s b --closing` sets `@`'s parents to `main` and the last rung and then commits:
  the closing as the merge close-out, its first parent the current `main`, its second the last
  rung. The " closing" and " dead-end closing" title suffixes are checked against the flag, never
  its trigger.
- `vc-x1 install` runs `[install] release` after checking that `@-` is `main` at `main@origin`,
  `@` is empty, and the version is bare, and `vc-x1 install --dev` runs `[install] dev` with no
  check, the mid-cycle refresh of the dev binary.
- `vc-x1 run-dev` runs `[install] dev-bin` with the given arguments from any directory of the
  workspace, and warns when the binary's `-V` is not the manifest's version.

#### Acceptance check

In a scratch dual workspace made by the dev binary's `init`: `commit -s b` makes a pair whose
trailers name each other, a `squash -s b` after a further edit in each repo folds both and leaves
the trailers valid, `push -s b` publishes the pair unchanged and refuses while the work `@` holds
an edit, and each of the five commands without `-s` exits non-zero naming the four scopes.
`commit -s b --closing` on a bookmark of two rungs makes a merge whose parents are the fork point
and the second rung, and a `squash -s b` into it keeps both. On a plain jj repo, `commit -s p` and
`push -s p` commit and publish with no trailer.
`install` refuses, or warns, when `@-` is not `main` at `main@origin`, and `install --dev` leaves
`tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1` at the manifest's version. `run-dev -V` prints the manifest's version. In this
workspace, two full `validate` runs at different versions leave one binary under `tmp/dev`, its

- Multi-step, a trapezoid the default, the agent's proposal and wink's go at the bookmark, eight

#### Problem

What the user reviews is not what is published. A rung's commit exists only once `vc-x1 push` has
made and published it, so a fix after the review of its description is a remote rewrite and a
squash-push in both repos. The closing is changed twice more after its review, at Land: the
package's plain name is squashed back into it, and the trapezoid recipe reshapes it into the merge.
The rename exists because a mid-cycle `cargo install` would otherwise replace the consumers'
binary, and Land's promotion itself names no command.

#### Solution

Provisional, the Todo's plan as filed:

- An `[install]` table in the config: `release`, the promotion,
  `["cargo install --path . --locked"]` here, `dev`, the dev install,
  `["cargo install --path . --locked --root tmp/dev"]` here, both lists like `[validate]`'s, and
  `dev-bin`, the dev install's binary, `"tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1"` here. `.vc-config.md`'s
  `[validate] full` ends with the dev install's line. The stale `vc-config.md` examples are fixed
  with the keys, fast's `["cargo test --bins"]`, full's `cargo test` without
  `-- --include-ignored`, and `test.fixtures`' `"../vc-x1-fixtures"` with its "skips with a notice"
  prose, and `vc-config-model.md` is regenerated.
- A scope resolver shared by `commit`, `squash`, `push`, `squash-push`, and `sync`: `-s`, required,
  one of `work|w`, `agent|a`, `both|b`, or `por|p`, a plain repo with no pair, and `-R` optional,
  the workspace by its root or either repo for `w|a|b`, the repo itself for `p`, the cwd without
  it. No `-s` is an error naming the four. `-s p` on a repo that is one side of a dual workspace is
  an error naming the side, and `-s w|a|b` on a directory with no workspace config is one.
- `vc-x1 commit -s b` makes the rung's commit pair from the two working copies, each stamped with
  the other's change id, with the given title and body. `-s w` and `-s a` are errors in a dual
  workspace, since a half is an unpaired commit, and `-s p` commits a plain repo with no trailer.
- `vc-x1 squash` folds each scoped working copy into its side of the pair, the review's fix into
  the work commit and the review's transcript into the agent commit, and refuses a side whose
  commit is published. With `--title` and `--body` it rewrites both descriptions and restamps the
  trailers, the one sanctioned re-describe of a trailer-carrying commit.
- `vc-x1 push` only publishes: the work bookmark `@-` sits on, and the agent-repo's `main`. Its
  agent half folds the agent `@` first, the journal's last lines, and its work half refuses a
  non-empty `@`, which is a `squash` or the next rung, the user's call. `--title`, `--body`, and the
  bookmark argument go, the bookmark inferred from `@-` and named only as a check.
- `vc-x1 squash-push` stays, wink's most-used command, `squash-push -s a` the agent half of a push
  on its own, and `-s w|b` the fold-and-publish that asks nothing.
- `vc-x1 merge -s w --target <rev> --from <revset>...` adds the sources to one target's parents,
  with jj's rebase meaning, refusing a target in jj's `immutable()` unless `--ignore-immutable`.
  `vc-x1 commit -s b --closing` sets `@`'s parents to `main` and the last rung and then commits:
  the closing as the merge close-out, its first parent the current `main`, its second the last
  rung. The " closing" and " dead-end closing" title suffixes are checked against the flag, never
  its trigger.
- `vc-x1 install` runs `[install] release` after checking that `@-` is `main` at `main@origin`,
  `@` is empty, and the version is bare, and `vc-x1 install --dev` runs `[install] dev` with no
  check, the mid-cycle refresh of the dev binary.
- `vc-x1 run-dev` runs `[install] dev-bin` with the given arguments from any directory of the
  workspace, and warns when the binary's `-V` is not the manifest's version.

I made both changes. Full validation passed on the second run. The first stopped on a clippy lint in the new tests, three `[x.clone()]` slice literals, which I changed to `std::slice::from_ref`.

**What changed:**
- **`-s a` and `-s b` with `--yes` (or `-y`):**
  - Without the flag they're refused, and the message names `--yes`.
  - With it, each repo in the scope moves the same bookmark name, and the target is resolved in each repo, so `@-` means each repo's own `@-`.
  - Every repo is checked before any bookmark moves. If the name or the target is missing in one repo, nothing moves in either.
  - If a later move fails after an earlier one succeeded, the repos already moved are restored from their snapshots.
- **`-s p` requires `-R`** and uses that repo as given, with no workspace config lookup and no refusal when it's one side of a dual workspace. The bookmark-exists, one-commit, and backward checks still apply, as you picked.
- **Code shape:** each repo gets a plan step for the checks, then the moves run, so a scope of one or two repos takes the same path.
- **Docs:** `main.rs`'s long help, the README section with two new examples, and the record's Solution bullet and rung subsection.

**Tests (6):**
- the required flags
- the scopes: `a` and `b` refused without `--yes`, then resolving to the agent repo and to both; `w` from the agent side resolving to the work repo; `p` refused without `-R`, and accepted on one side of a dual workspace
- forward moves
- both repos' `main` moving, and a missing bookmark or target in one repo stopping both
- backward and sideways moves needing the flag
- refusals and a dry run

**Tried with the dev binary on this repo:**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `-s b` without `--yes` | Refused, naming `--yes` |
| `-s b --yes --dry-run` | Work `main` would fast-forward to the cycle tip, and the agent `main` is already at its `@-`, so it's left alone |
| `-s p` without `-R` | Refused |
| `-s p -R .agent-session` | Used as given, and `main` is already there |
